original_question: Let X be a Banach space. Must the following semi-Eberlein dual-ball statements hold: (1) if X has a norming Markushevich basis, then (B_{X*}, w*) is semi-Eberlein; (2) if (B_{X*}, w*) is semi-Eberlein for every equivalent renorming of X, then X is a subspace of a weakly compactly generated Banach space; and (3) if K_ϱ is the compact space obtained as the closure of F_ϱ = {F_n(α) : n < ω, α < ω1} in the pointwise topology of P(ω1), where F_n(α) = {ξ ≤ α : ϱ(ξ, α) ≤ n}, then are the dual balls of C([0, ω1]) and C(K_ϱ) semi-Eberlein?
target_in_paper: Problem 7.4 in Section 7: the three-part open problem about when weak* dual balls are semi-Eberlein, with the notation Kϱ taken from the construction in Section 4. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2402.18442))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper. It captures all three numbered parts of the official problem, correctly centers the weak* dual ball in items (1) and (2), and correctly identifies Kϱ through the closure of Fϱ built from the ordinal metric ϱ. It also keeps the two specific test spaces C([0, ω1]) and C(Kϱ) that appear verbatim in the paper’s item (3). ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2402.18442))
missing_details: The nearest official target is not a conjecture or theorem from the introduction but the explicitly stated open problem Problem 7.4 in Section 7. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2402.18442))

To be stand-alone, the question should define semi-Eberlein: a compact space K is semi-Eberlein iff it is homeomorphic to a compact subset L of [-1,1]^Γ for some set Γ such that L ∩ c0(Γ) is dense in L. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2402.18442))

To be stand-alone, the question should define a norming Markushevich basis, or at least say that it is a biorthogonal system {eα; φα}α∈Γ with dense span of the vectors, weak*-dense span of the functionals, and with span{φα} norming in X*. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2402.18442))

Item (2) should explicitly quantify over equivalent norms on the same underlying linear space X, so that the renormed weak* dual ball is the object being tested each time. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2402.18442))

Item (3) should explicitly mention the weak* topology on the dual balls, i.e. (BC([0, ω1])*, w*) and (BC(Kϱ)*, w*), since semi-Eberlein is a topological property of those compact spaces. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2402.18442))

For Kϱ, the paper assumes that ϱ:[ω1]^2→ω is an ordinal metric satisfying the four conditions (ϱ1)–(ϱ4) of Proposition 4.8; your draft gives Fn(α) but omits those hypotheses on ϱ. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2402.18442))
If the definition of Kϱ is included, it should also say that P(ω1) is identified with {0,1}^ω1 and carries the pointwise/product topology. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2402.18442))

The official wording in item (3) is 'Are the dual balls of C([0, ω1]) or C(Kϱ) semi-Eberlein?'; your 'and' can be read as a slightly stronger joint requirement than the paper’s phrasing. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2402.18442))

For paper-faithful scope, it is helpful to note that Remark 7.3 already proves the positive result for 1-norming M-bases, so the genuine open part of item (1) is the passage from 1-norming to merely norming M-bases. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2402.18442))
refined_question: Let X be a Banach space, and write (BX*, w*) for its dual unit ball with the weak* topology. Recall that a compact space K is called semi-Eberlein if it is homeomorphic to a compact subset L ⊆ [-1,1]^Γ for some set Γ such that L ∩ c0(Γ) is dense in L. Suppose X admits a norming Markushevich basis {eα; φα}α∈Γ, meaning that {eα; φα}α∈Γ is a biorthogonal system with span{eα} dense in X, span{φα} weak*-dense in X*, and span{φα} norming in X*. Must (BX*, w*) be semi-Eberlein? More generally, if for every equivalent norm ||·||' on the underlying linear space X the renormed weak* dual ball (B(X,||·||')*, w*) is semi-Eberlein, must X be a subspace of a weakly compactly generated Banach space? Finally, let ϱ:[ω1]^2→ω satisfy conditions (ϱ1)–(ϱ4) of Proposition 4.8, define Fn(α) = {ξ ≤ α : ϱ(ξ, α) ≤ n} for n < ω and α < ω1, let Fϱ = {Fn(α) : n < ω, α < ω1}, and let Kϱ be the closure of Fϱ in the pointwise topology of P(ω1) = {0,1}^ω1. Are the dual balls of C([0, ω1]) or C(Kϱ) semi-Eberlein? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2402.18442))
justification: This draft is targeting Section 7, not the introductory problems. Section 7 first defines semi-Eberlein compacta in Definition 7.1, then records in Remark 7.3 that a 1-norming M-basis already yields a semi-Eberlein dual ball, and immediately after states exactly the three-part open problem that your draft is trying to capture, namely Problem 7.4. The references to C([0, ω1]) and C(Kϱ) are also paper-faithful: Section 5 singles out C([0, ω1]) as a key test case and proves it has no norming M-basis, while Section 4 introduces Kϱ and the Banach-space construction inside C(Kϱ). ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2402.18442))
